target.name: example-rule-skill
target.purpose: Turn one source-backed decision into an executable rule.

sources.authority: Defines the requested outcome and scope.
claims: The skill must produce an observable deliverable.

rules.decision: Whether the requested deliverable is complete.
rules.trigger: After the skill produces its target artifact.
rules.action: Inspect the artifact against the declared acceptance signal.
rules.acceptance: The artifact exists and satisfies its task-specific contract.
rules.rationale: A rule changes behavior only when its result can be checked.

placements.reason: The executor needs the acceptance signal on every run.

checks.name: authority_traceability
evidence: Replace this example with target-specific source evidence.

checks.name: rule_closure
evidence: Replace this example with a target-specific closure review.

checks.name: merge_safety
evidence: Record the equivalence comparison or why no merge candidates exist.

checks.name: abstraction_preservation
evidence: Record the abstraction review or why abstraction is not applicable.

checks.name: runtime_reachability
evidence: Record how the direct consumer reaches the rule.

checks.name: structural_validation
evidence: Record parser, link, script, and package validation results.

checks.name: behavior_positive
evidence: Record a realistic positive behavior test.

checks.name: behavior_boundary
evidence: Record a neighboring request that must not misroute.

checks.name: behavior_conflict
evidence: Record a conflict, authorized override, state override, or degradation-path test.
